'''Robert Luis Santos''' (born 1957) is an American [[statistician]] who was the [[director of the United States Census Bureau]] from 2022 to 2025. He served as the 116th president of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=ASA Members Elect Robert Santos, Dionne Price to Association Leadership |url=https://www.amstat.org/asa/News/ASA-Members-Elect-Robert-Santos-Dionne-Price-to-Association-Leadership.aspx |website=www.amstat.org |access-date=13 December 2021 |archive-date=21 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211121204412/https://www.amstat.org/asa/News/ASA-Members-Elect-Robert-Santos-Dionne-Price-to-Association-Leadership.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Santos was born in [[San Antonio]]. After graduating from [[Holy Cross of San Antonio]], he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in mathematics from [[Trinity University (Texas)|Trinity University]] and a Master of Arts in statistics from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 13, 2021|title=President Biden Announces His Intent to Nominate Robert Santos for Director of the U.S. Census Bureau|url=https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2021/04/13/president-biden-announces-his-intent-to-nominate-robert-santos-for-director-of-the-u-s-census-bureau/|access-date=April 13, 2021|website=The White House|language=en-US|archive-date=April 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413192154/https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2021/04/13/president-biden-announces-his-intent-to-nominate-robert-santos-for-director-of-the-u-s-census-bureau/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Career ==
Santos has worked at the University of Michigan's Survey Research Center, [[NORC at the University of Chicago]], and the Institute for Survey Research at [[Temple University]]. He was the 116th president of the [[American Statistical Association]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=ASA Members Elect Robert Santos, Dionne Price to Association Leadership|url=https://www.amstat.org/asa/News/ASA-Members-Elect-Robert-Santos-Dionne-Price-to-Association-Leadership.aspx|access-date=2021-05-20|website=amstat.org|language=en|archive-date=2021-05-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210520190940/https://www.amstat.org/asa/News/ASA-Members-Elect-Robert-Santos-Dionne-Price-to-Association-Leadership.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref> 2013-2014 president of the [[American Association for Public Opinion Research|American Association of Public Opinion Research]], and a member of the [[National Center for Health Statistics]] board of counselors.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Wang |first1=Hansi Lo |title=Biden To Make Historic Census Director Pick With Latinx Statistician Rob Santos|url=https://www.npr.org/2021/04/13/986612530/biden-to-make-historic-census-director-pick-with-latinx-statistician-rob-santos|access-date=2021-04-13|website=NPR|date=13 April 2021 |language=en|archive-date=2021-04-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413191621/https://www.npr.org/2021/04/13/986612530/biden-to-make-historic-census-director-pick-with-latinx-statistician-rob-santos|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Gonzalez|first=Oriana|title=Biden picks Robert Santos to be first person of color to lead Census bureau|url=https://www.axios.com/biden-robert-santos-census-bureau-04e1f97c-bf88-4547-83ac-215e6e55eaba.html|access-date=2021-04-13|website=Axios|date=13 April 2021|language=en|archive-date=2021-04-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413202342/https://www.axios.com/biden-robert-santos-census-bureau-04e1f97c-bf88-4547-83ac-215e6e55eaba.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Santos was the vice president for statistical methods and chief methodologist at the [[Urban Institute]]<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2016-06-04|title=Robert Santos|url=https://www.urban.org/author/robert-santos|access-date=2021-04-13|journal=Urban Institute|language=en|archive-date=2021-04-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413223615/https://www.urban.org/author/robert-santos|url-status=live}}</ref> in Washington, D.C.

Santos was confirmed as United States Census Bureau Director by the U.S. Senate on November 4, 2021,<ref>Michael Macagnone. [https://www.rollcall.com/2021/11/04/senate-confirms-new-census-bureau-director/ Senate confirms new Census Bureau director] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211105152035/https://www.rollcall.com/2021/11/04/senate-confirms-new-census-bureau-director/ |date=2021-11-05 }}, ''[[Roll Call]]'', 4 Nov 2021</ref> and was sworn in on January 5, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Robert Santos |url=https://www.census.gov/newsroom/bios/robert-santos.html |website=United States Census Bureau |access-date=6 January 2022 |archive-date=5 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220105211141/https://www.census.gov/newsroom/bios/robert-santos.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Santos is of [[Mexican Americans|Mexican American]] heritage. He is the first Latino person to serve as permanent, Senate-approved director of the Census Bureau (James F. Holmes, a Black man, was acting director of the Census Bureau in January-October 1998).<ref>{{Cite web |author=Wang, Hansi Lo |date=2021-11-04 |title=The Senate has confirmed the 1st Latino to lead the U.S. census, Robert Santos |url=https://www.npr.org/2021/11/04/1014670567/first-latino-census-director-robert-santos-person-of-color |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201203447/https://www.npr.org/2021/11/04/1014670567/first-latino-census-director-robert-santos-person-of-color |archive-date=2022-02-01 |access-date=2022-02-01 |website=NPR |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2006 Santos was recipient of the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]].<ref name=ASAFoundersAward>{{cite web | title=Founders Award | publisher=American Statistical Association | url=https://www.amstat.org/your-career/awards/founders-award }}</ref>

In 2023 he was awarded an honorary doctorate by [[North Carolina State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honorary Degrees Conferred |url=https://leadership.ncsu.edu/board-of-trustees/honorary-degrees/degrees-conferred/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250418211906/https://leadership.ncsu.edu/board-of-trustees/honorary-degrees/degrees-conferred/ |archive-date=2025-04-18 |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=University Leadership |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Santos identifies as a [[Chicano]]. From 2012 to 2019, he was a [[South by Southwest|SXSW]] Festival photographer and later helped manage the photo crew of about 100 photographers at this annual film and music event in Austin.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Census director is a Chicano who photographed bands at SXSW and used tortilla dough to fish |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/census-director-chicano-photographed-bands-sxsw-used-tortilla-dough-fi-rcna44602 |access-date=September 27, 2023 |website=NBS News Latino |date=28 August 2022 |archive-date=27 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230927133014/https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/census-director-chicano-photographed-bands-sxsw-used-tortilla-dough-fi-rcna44602 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=What Does Rob Santos Like to Do When He Is Not Being a Statistician? |url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/01/01/pastimes-santos/ |access-date=September 27, 2023 |website=AMSTAT News |date=January 2018 |archive-date=September 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230927133007/https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/01/01/pastimes-santos/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
